en: Now begins the Śrī Bharata Kavaca from within the illustrious Ānanda Rāmāyaṇa.
Agastya said:
Hereafter, I shall tell you the armor (kavaca) of Bharata, which removes all sins, is meritorious, and always bestows devotion to Śrī Rāma. || 1 ||
O best of the Raghus, [I salute] that dark-complexioned son of Kaikeyī who always gazes upon you, who is devoted to the word of the beloved of the daughter of Videha, the lord of the seven islands,
and who stands holding a beautiful chowrie near the left side of Śrī Sītā’s husband.
I worship him who, holding Bharata with his right hand, is fanning him. || 2 ||
Of this mantra of the Śrī Bharata-kavaca, Agastya is the seer (ṛṣi),
Śrī Bharata is the deity (devatā),
and Anuṣṭubh is the meter (chandaḥ).
"Śaṅkha" is the seed-syllable (bīja);
"delight of Kaikeyī" is the power (śakti);
"lord of the Bharata region" is the peg (kīlaka).
"Rāmānuja" is the weapon-mantra;
"Saptadvīpeśvaradāsa" is the armor-mantra;
and "Rāmāṃśaja" is the core mantra.
The application is for the sake of pleasing Śrī Bharata and for the fulfillment of all desires during the recitation.
Now follows the ritual placement of the fingers (aṅgulīnyāsa).
Oṃ, homage to Bharata with the two thumbs; Oṃ, homage to Śaṅkha with the two index fingers;
Oṃ, homage to Kaikeyīnandana with the two middle fingers.
Oṃ, obeisance to the Lord of Bharatakhaṇḍa with the two ring fingers.
Oṃ, obeisance to the younger brother of Rāma with the two little fingers. Oṃ, obeisance to the servant of the Lord of the seven continents with the palms and backs of the hands.
The ritual placement (nyāsa) of the heart and other [limbs].
Oṃ, homage to Bharata, the heart; Oṃ, svāhā to Śaṅkha, the head;
Oṃ, vaṣaṭ to Kaikeyīnandana, the tuft of hair.
Oṃ, to the Lord of Bharatakhaṇḍa, for the armor, hūṃ! Oṃ, to the younger brother of Rāma, for the three eyes, vauṣaṭ!
Oṃ, to the servant of the Lord of the seven islands, for the weapon, phaṭ!
Oṃ, you who are born from a portion of Rāma—thus is the binding of the directions.
Now, meditation.
On the left side of Rāmacandra stood the son of Kekayī, charmingly fanning Rāma with a yak-tail whisk. || 1 ||
He is beautifully adorned with jeweled earrings, armlets, bracelets, and other ornaments;
he wears yellow garments and is resplendent with a forest garland. || 2 ||
Māṇḍavī beheld him whose feet were washed, who was adorned with a girdle and anklets, who was dark like the petal of a blue lotus, and whose face was like the king of birds (Garuḍa). || 3 ||
[He saw] the younger brother of Rāma, whose arms reached his knees, the protector of Bharatavarṣa, with a smiling face, and who was praised by Śatrughna. || 4 ||
I bow to that auspicious Bharata, the great hero devoted to Rāma, whose glance was pleasing and gentle, and who possessed a splendor equal to a mass of lightning. || 5 ||
Having meditated thus upon Bharata, who has Rāma’s feet fixed in his heart,
this supreme armor of Bharata should indeed be recited.
The commencement of the Kavaca.
Oṃ! May Bharata protect from the east; may the son of Kaikeyī protect from the south; may the prince protect from the west; and may the best of the Raghus protect from the north. 1.

May he whose limbs are dark protect from below, may the son of Daśaratha protect from above, may the lord of Bhāratavarṣa protect the middle, and may he born of the solar dynasty protect everywhere. || 2 ||
May Śiva protect my head; may the beloved of Hari protect my forehead;
may the daughter of Janaka, who is solely intent on his words, protect the space between my eyebrows.
May the son-in-law of Janaka protect my eyes here always; may the beloved of Māṇḍavī protect my cheeks, and he of smiling countenance my root of the ear. 4.
May he who increases the joy of Kaikeyī protect my nose-tip always;
may he of noble limbs protect my face, and may the wearer of matted locks protect my speech. || 5 ||
May Puṣkaratāta protect my tongue; may the Radiant One protect my teeth; may the Wearer of Bark protect my chin; and may the Fair-faced One protect my throat. 6.
May he who has conquered his enemies protect my shoulders; may he who is saluted by Śatrughna protect my arms;
may the wearer of armor protect my hands, and may the wielder of the sword protect my nails.
May the younger brother of Rāma protect my belly; may the beloved of Śrī Rāma protect my chest;
may he who stands at the side of Rāghava protect my sides; and may the one of noble speech protect my back. || 8 ||
May the wielder of the bow protect the belly, and may the maker of arrows protect the navel;
may the lotus-eyed one protect the waist, and may he whose mind is fixed solely on Rāma protect the private parts.
May Rāmamitra protect my genitals; may the servant of Śrī Rāma protect my thighs; and may he who dwells in Nandigrāma protect my knees at all times. || 10 ||
May the wearer of the Śrī Rāma footprints always protect my shanks;
may the friend of Śrī Rāma protect my ankles, and may he who is worshipped by the gods protect my feet. || 11 ||
May the protector of Rāma's command protect my limbs here at all times;
may he, the ornament of Raghu’s lineage, protect the toes of my feet. || 12 ||
May the delightful one protect my body hairs; may the wise one protect me at night;
and may the bearer of the quiver protect my directions during the day at all times.
May Pañcajanya protect me at all times, always on this earth.
Thus, O Sutīkṣṇa, is this auspicious armor of Śrībharas.
Indeed, I have declared before you this hymn, which brings about great auspiciousness; it should be known as the supreme among all hymns, bestowing great merit. (15)
This armor of Bharata, which bestows joy upon Rāmacandra, should always be recited with devotion; having recited it, the delighter of the Raghus [bestowed it]. || 16 ||
Just as one attains supreme satisfaction by means of one's own armor, therefore this, the most excellent of all armors, should always be recited. || 17 ||
By reciting this here, a mortal shall attain all desires;
one desiring knowledge shall obtain knowledge, and one desiring a son shall obtain a son. (18)
One desiring a wife shall obtain a wife; one seeking wealth shall acquire wealth.
Whatever is longed for by the mind, all that is attained through the recitation of this armor (kavaca).
This is truly obtained by men here; I speak the truth, O devotee of Rāma: therefore, it should always be recited by men. (20)
Thus ends the Śrī Bharata-kavaca within the Manohara-kāṇḍa of the glorious Ānanda-rāmāyaṇa by Vālmīki, which is part of the illustrious Śatakoṭi-ramacarita.
